questions.q: Phenyl acetate is heated with anhydrous AlCl₃ at a LOW temperature and then worked up with aqueous acid. The major product is:
questions.explain: At low temperature the reaction is under kinetic control and para attack is faster and less hindered. Remember 'low–para, high–ortho'.

questions.q: At high temperature the ortho product dominates in the Fries rearrangement because:
options: the ortho position is less hindered than the para position
the o-hydroxy ketone forms a stable six-membered chelate with aluminium, making it the thermodynamic product
the acylium ion rearranges at high temperature
the reaction becomes purely intramolecular at high temperature
questions.explain: The OH and C=O oxygens of the ortho product both grip the aluminium, so at high temperature the reaction reaches this more stable product. The para product is the kinetic one.

questions.q: 4-Methylphenyl acetate (p-tolyl acetate) undergoes the Fries rearrangement with AlCl₃. The product is:
questions.explain: The para position is blocked by the methyl group, so the acyl group can only enter ortho to the OH, giving 2-hydroxy-5-methylacetophenone whatever the temperature.

questions.q: Phenol cannot be converted directly into a hydroxyaryl ketone by Friedel–Crafts acylation (RCOCl/AlCl₃) because:
options: phenol is too deactivated towards electrophiles
the phenolic oxygen reacts first, giving the phenyl ester
the acylium ion cannot form in the presence of phenol
questions.explain: Under these conditions phenol is acylated on oxygen, giving the ester; the Fries rearrangement is then needed to move the acyl group onto the ring. Phenol is activated, not deactivated.
